messages.subject: Marginalising out two discrete parameters
parts:
Hi,

I can, by hand, calculate the marginal density which I would like to sample from:

p(y|c,d) = sum(a=1,A) [sum(b=1,B) [ Uniform(a) Uniform(b) product(t=1,T) Poisson(y(t)| a, b, c, d) ] ]

Here a and b are discrete (and independent), whereas c and d are continuous.

However, when I try to calculate the log marginal density, as per the first example in chapter 11 of Stan's manual, I can't seem to get a quantity that I can work with in Stan. (I'm sure it's probably due to my ineptitude using the log_sum_exp function). 

At the moment I have tried:

log[p(y|c,d)] = log_sum_exp(a=1,A) [ log(Uniform(a)) + log(sum(b=1,B) [Uniform(b) + log (Poisson(y(t)| a, b, c, d))]]

However, I am getting caught on the second part, since I have the log of a sum again (this time for B). Is there a way to use log_sum_exp again, to get a Stan-workable expression? I have tried this, but seem to end up with log log Poisson expressions...

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Marginalising out two discrete parameters
parts:
The simplest thing to do is this:

matrix[A,B] lp;
lp <- rep_matrix(0, A, B);
for (a in 1:A)
for (b in 1:B)
for (t in 1:T)
lp[m,n] <- lp[m,n] + log prob of y(t) given a, b, c, d

increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(to_vector(lp)));

That is, you need to marginalize both out jointly. Better to
just do the log_sum_exp once for efficiency, though you can
nest:

log_sum_exp({a, b, c, d})

= log_sum_exp(log_sum_exp(a, b), log_sum_exp(c, d));

= log(exp(a) + exp(b) + ... + exp(d))

- Bob
